title: Local- and regional-scale air pollution modelling (PM(10)) and exposure assessment for pregnancy trimesters, infancy, and childhood to age 15 years: Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents And Children (ALSPAC).
ehr_evidence: ALSPAC provided us with all residential addresses held in the ALSPAC contact database (n = 45,771); we downloaded hourly concentrations of PM10 from the AURN data archive for the Bristol Centre and Bristol St Paul's monitoring sites. The study used dispersion modelling (ADMS-Urban, NAME-III) of PM10, not electronic health records.
summary: A PM10 exposure-modelling study using ADMS-Urban and NAME-III dispersion models to estimate source-specific particulate exposures across pregnancy trimesters, infancy, and childhood to age ~15 in the ALSPAC birth cohort (Bristol/Avon, England).
key_findings: Model evaluation: ST-PM10TOTAL correlated with weekly measured PM10 at the Bristol Centre site (r = 0.71, p = 0.000), MSE-r2 = 0.41, RMSE = 11.4 μg/m3, MB = -4.1 μg/m3, MPB = 21%, FAC2 = 81% (n = 37 weeks).
Mean ST-PM10TOTAL exposure was 33.5 μg/m3 (5th-95th centile 25.7-42.6) in trimester 1, declining to 30.8 μg/m3 (25.9-35.8) in late infancy.
Local main roads (ROAD) contributed ~3% (2.9-3.0%) of total PM10; regional/long-range (NAME) contributed 42.2-45.6%; local sources (ROAD+GRID) contributed 18.6-19.5%.
Mean long-term PM10 exposures fell from 31.2 μg/m3 (year 1) to 19.6 μg/m3 (age ~15), with a 5.4 μg/m3 difference between ages 0-8 (27.9 μg/m3) and 9-16 (22.5 μg/m3).
Spatial contrasts were low (5th-95th centile 25.4-30.0 μg/m3 to age ~8; 20.7-23.9 μg/m3 from age ~8 to ~15), and 9.5% of address locations were within 50 m of a main road.
captured_features: Modelled PM10 concentrations (μg/m3) by exposure period (trimesters, early/late infancy, annual to age ~15)
Source components: local main roads (ROAD), local other sources (GRID), regional/long-range (NAME), natural/background
Residential address history and geocoded coordinates
Model performance statistics (Spearman rho, MSE-r2, RMSE, MB, MPB, FAC2)
study_design: Cohort-based exposure assessment / dispersion-modelling methodology study (ALSPAC birth cohort)
population: ALSPAC birth cohort; pregnancies due to deliver 1991-1992 in Bristol/Avon, south west England; children followed from conception to age ~15 years (n = 11,929 for pregnancy/infancy; n = 10,383 to age ~15)
limitations: Model evaluation limited to a single monitoring site at any time (1993-2008), so spatial bias could not be quantified.
No information on individual point sources (e.g. industrial stacks) for earlier years; aggregated 1 km grid emissions used.
SO2 emissions not included, so secondary sulphate chemistry was unaccounted for, possibly underestimating local PM10.
Terrain and building effects not modelled; single constant (12.0 μg/m3) used for natural sources.
Limited monitoring data for pregnancy periods (1990-1992) required imputation; study area excluded participants who moved far from the catchment.
